title: A Tide for the Garden
premise: Juniper Okafor inherits half of a failing orchard from the grandmother he barely knew—only to discover the other half belongs to Wren Ashby, the childhood friend his family cut ties with a decade ago. Forced to share the land through one harvest season, Juniper bakes at his struggling café by day and fights Wren over every fence line by night, until the arguments turn into something neither will name. When a developer's offer could save Juniper's café but erase the orchard, he must choose between the safe, containable life he built and the found family gathering in Wren's cider shed. On festival night, Juniper lets the last train leave without him—and signs the deed as a partnership instead of a partition.
about_author: Emrys Thackeray is a former orchard laborer turned novelist who writes love stories set in places where the soil remembers more than the people do. He lives near the coast with his partner and an untidy garden he refuses to fence.

chapters.title: The Deed That Argues Back
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Three missed payments deep, Juniper receives a solicitor's letter: he's inherited half of Marlowe Orchard, co-owned with Wren Ashby, the boy his mother forbade him from seeing after a family rupture he never fully understood. Arriving at the orchard, he finds Wren living in the cider shed, equally furious. The emotional beat is defensive shock—the heart as a locked muscle, tested at the door.

chapters.title: Forty Rows of Grudges
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Forced into a working truce, Juniper and Wren split the orchard down the middle and sabotage each other's harvest plans while old letters reveal their grandmothers were secret partners—and something more. Juniper's café regulars begin drifting up the hill to help, forming an accidental crew. The emotional beat is grudging warmth: rivalry softening into ritual, and the first almost-confession.

chapters.title: What the Developer Knew
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A developer arrives with an offer that would clear Juniper's café debt and pay them both handsomely—Wren, drowning in back taxes, is tempted. Juniper, wounded by Wren's hesitation, retreats behind the counter and nearly signs alone. A storm flattens the east rows, and the found family shows up with tarps at midnight. The emotional beat is the climax: Wren chooses the orchard and, in front of everyone, chooses Juniper.

chapters.title: The Last Train, Missed on Purpose
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Festival night: cider, lanterns, and the deed spread on a cider-press table. Juniper declines the developer, refinances the café with the orchard as collateral, and signs as co-steward with Wren. He lets the last train leave without him and says the thing he trained his heart never to say. The emotional beat is resolution—inheritance redefined as belonging, and a home with two names on the door.
